caption: Turns a fast clock into a slow one: the output stays on for 3 input pulses, then off for 3, so it ticks 3 times slower with an even on/off split. Detail: a ring of 3 droppers passing one item around, one step per input edge (an observer fires it on both edges), and a copper bulb that flips each time the item comes back around; part of a family for any odd N

While the input is held on it beats like a metronome, one short pulse every 8 ticks, and it stops as soon as the input goes off. Detail: a comparator in subtract mode whose own output comes back to its side through dust and a delay-1 repeater, so it switches itself off and on again; the first pulse comes right after the input turns on

One press gives exactly two pulses: a copper bulb notices the press, and a short delay plus a second observer turn that one event into two blips. Detail: the bulb toggles on each rising edge, its comparator changes, an observer makes that a 2 tick pulse, a delay-3 repeater stretches it to 6 ticks, and a second observer pulses on both of the repeater's edges

One press gives exactly three pulses: the two-pulse bulb burst plus one more observer stage that adds a third blip. Detail: bulb, comparator, observer, delay-3 repeater, observer, then an observer watching the second observer toggles a second bulb whose own observers add the third pulse

One press gives exactly four pulses: one detected press is split into four copies that arrive at different times, like echoes, all into the same output. Detail: a bulb edge detector (bulb, comparator, observer) whose pulse fans out through observers, a second bulb and a torch into four delayed taps; any input length

While the input is held on, two observers stare at each other and keep firing, a pulse every 4 ticks; it stops when the input goes off. Detail: 3 blocks: the input extends a sticky piston that pushes one observer face to face with the other (the chase), and retracting it breaks the pair apart

One press gives exactly 2 pulses: the press holds two observers face to face for a fixed moment, and they fire at each other 2 times before being pulled apart. Detail: a bulb edge detector (bulb, comparator, observer) and a repeater hold a sticky piston out for a fixed time; the piston pushes an observer face to face with another and they chase (a pulse every 4 ticks) until it retracts

One press gives exactly 3 pulses: the press holds two observers face to face for a fixed moment, and they fire at each other 3 times before being pulled apart. Detail: a bulb edge detector (bulb, comparator, observer) and a repeater hold a sticky piston out for a fixed time; the piston pushes an observer face to face with another and they chase (a pulse every 4 ticks) until it retracts

The input's dust points into the empty cell X beside the output. A delay-3 repeater (6 gt) and two dust power a sticky piston that pushes a stone into X: the output is lit only while the stone is in X AND the input still powers it, so an input shorter than the repeater delay plus the piston's travel never lights it, and a longer one lights it for its length - 8 gt, going dark in the same tick as the input (the sticky piston pulls the stone back while the dust is already off). The repeater makes every piston pulse at least 6 gt, so the piston never spits its stone.

Two comparator rings (crates/circuit-timer/src/long.rs). Stage 1 (two comparators, round 4 gt): the input beside the corner dust of stage 1's return line holds stage 1 up; once its charge stops it decays 2 per round, so its output lasts at least 28 gt. A repeater reading its stone A1 powers stage 2's stone I2: stage 2 is a ring of 3 comparators (round 6 gt) that loses 1 per round, refilled evenly at 15 by stage 1's long output; once stage 1 dies it counts its levels down, and the output lamp beside its stone A2 goes dark at 0.

Divides a fast clock by 3 (one output pulse for every 3 input pulses) and keeps up with clocks as fast as a pulse every 8 ticks, where the item-ring dividers stop at 10. Detail: three copper bulbs in a ring with exactly one lit; every input pulse passes the lit one on to the next (each step: the bulb's comparator gates a short edge pulse), and the output reads one of them
